title: Approximation of an isomorphism of completed local rings by pointed etale neighborhoods
statement: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], let $X,Y$ be schemes locally of finite type over $S$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $x\in X$, $y\in Y$ lie over $s\in S$. Assume $\mathcal O_{S,s}$ is a G-ring [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. Given an $\mathcal O_{S,s}$-algebra isomorphism $\varphi:\widehat{\mathcal O}_{Y,y}\xrightarrow{\sim}\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,x}$ of completed local rings [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], for every integer $N\geq2$ there are morphisms $(X,x)\leftarrow(U,u)\to(Y,y)$ of pointed schemes over $S$ such that both arrows are etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] and induce isomorphisms $\kappa(x)\to\kappa(u)$ and $\kappa(y)\to\kappa(u)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. These are the elementary etale neighbourhood conditions. Moreover, the two maps from $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{Y,y}$ to $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{U,u}$, one induced by $U\to Y$ and the other obtained by following $\varphi$ with the map induced by $U\to X$, agree modulo $\mathfrak m_u^N\widehat{\mathcal O}_{U,u}$, where $\mathfrak m_u$ is the maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_{U,u}$.

proof.text: Fix $N\geq2$. Restrict $\varphi$ to the canonical image of $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ in its completion, obtaining the local $\mathcal O_{S,s}$-map $\theta:\mathcal O_{Y,y}\to\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,x}$. Apply [lem-trf-local-map-completion-approximation] to this map with the given $N$. This gives $p:(U,u)\to(X,x)$ etale with unchanged residue field, and an $S$-map $f:(U,u)\to(Y,y)$ with the required congruence on $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$. The hypotheses are exactly the given locally Noetherian base, the two locally finite type structural maps, and the G-ring $\mathcal O_{S,s}$.

source.place: Tag 0CAV, first sentence, applying Tag 0CAU to the restriction of the given isomorphism

proof.text: Write $A=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$, $B=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, and $C=\mathcal O_{U,u}$. These rings are Noetherian: take affine finite-type charts over a Noetherian affine neighbourhood of $s$, use [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], and localize using [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-ring-maps] (its Noetherian-localization assertion, applied also to identity maps). For $U$ use affine charts of the etale map $p$; finite presentation implies finite type. The map $p_u^{\sharp}:B\to C$ is flat by [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-flat-morphism]. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-prime-generates-maximal] on these etale affine charts it satisfies $\mathfrak m_B C=\mathfrak m_C$, and Step 1 supplies the residue-field isomorphism. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-completion-iso] gives an isomorphism $\widehat p^{\sharp}:\widehat B\xrightarrow{\sim}\widehat C$. Put $\alpha=\widehat p^{\sharp}\circ\varphi:\widehat A\xrightarrow{\sim}\widehat C$ and let $g=\widehat f^{\sharp}:\widehat A\to\widehat C$ be the actual map induced by $f$.

source.place: Tag 0CAV, proof, invocation of More on Algebra Tag 0AGX (lemma-flat-unramified)

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak n_A=\mathfrak m_A\widehat A$ and $\mathfrak n_C=\mathfrak m_C\widehat C$. These are the maximal ideals by [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring]. For each $r\geq1$, [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-quotient] applied to $A\twoheadrightarrow A/\mathfrak m_A^r$ gives $\widehat A/\mathfrak n_A^r\cong A/\mathfrak m_A^r$: the quotient has nilpotent maximal ideal, so its defining completion sequence is constant from level $r$ onwards. In particular every $a\in\widehat A$ has a representative $a_0\in A$ with $a-a_0\in\mathfrak n_A^N$. Both $g$ and $\alpha$ are local maps and send this difference into $\mathfrak n_C^N$. Step 1 gives $g(a_0)-\alpha(a_0)\in\mathfrak n_C^N$, hence $g(a)-\alpha(a)\in\mathfrak n_C^N$ for every $a\in\widehat A$. This proves the claimed congruence on the whole completed source, rather than only on its dense local subring.

source.place: Tag 0CAV, congruence diagram on completions; extension of the Tag 0CAU congruence using completion of quotients, Algebra Tag 00MA

proof.text: Identify $\widehat A$ with $D=\widehat C$ using $\alpha$ and set $h=g\circ\alpha^{-1}:D\to D$. Thus $h(a)-a\in\mathfrak n^2$ for every $a\in D$, where $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak n_C$, because $N\geq2$. It follows that $h$ is the identity on $D/\mathfrak n$ and on $\mathfrak n/\mathfrak n^2$. More explicitly, for $a_1,\ldots,a_r\in\mathfrak n$, the telescoping expansion of $\prod_i h(a_i)-\prod_i a_i$ has in each term one factor in $\mathfrak n^2$ and $r-1$ factors in $\mathfrak n$, so it belongs to $\mathfrak n^{r+1}$. Every element of $\mathfrak n^r$ is a finite sum of such products: scalar coefficients can be absorbed into one factor. Hence $h$ acts as the identity on every $\mathfrak n^r/\mathfrak n^{r+1}$. This is the generation-in-degree-one argument for the associated graded ring, with the degree-zero case stated separately.

source.place: Tag 0CAV, associated-graded diagram and generation in degree 1

proof.text: For $r\geq1$ let $h_r:D/\mathfrak n^r\to D/\mathfrak n^r$ be induced by $h$. Inductively these maps are bijective. The base $r=1$ is Step 4. For injectivity at $r+1$, an element killed by $h_{r+1}$ reduces to zero modulo $\mathfrak n^r$ by injectivity of $h_r$, and is then zero in $\mathfrak n^r/\mathfrak n^{r+1}$ because $h$ is the identity there. For surjectivity, given $d\bmod\mathfrak n^{r+1}$ first choose $a$ with $h(a)\equiv d\bmod\mathfrak n^r$. The error $d-h(a)$ has a class in $\mathfrak n^r/\mathfrak n^{r+1}$; choose a representative $e\in\mathfrak n^r$ of that class. Step 4 gives $h(e)\equiv e\bmod\mathfrak n^{r+1}$, so $a+e$ is a preimage. This is an explicit chase of the two short exact sequences used by the source.

source.place: Tag 0CAV, final paragraph: induction with the short exact sequences of successive quotients

proof.text: The ideal $\mathfrak m_C$ is finitely generated since $C$ is Noetherian. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal] makes $D=\widehat C$ complete for $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak m_CD$. By [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], $D=\varprojlim_rD/\mathfrak n^r$. The inverse maps $h_r^{-1}$ of Step 5 commute with the transition quotients: both possible composites are inverses of the same commutative square of the $h_r$. Applying them coordinate by coordinate therefore defines an inverse ring map to $h$ on the compatible sequences. Hence $h$ is an isomorphism and so is $g=h\circ\alpha$. No unproved exactness of inverse limits is required.

source.place: Tag 0CAV, last sentence: isomorphisms of all infinitesimal quotients give the isomorphism on completions

proof.text: The map $f:U\to Y$ is locally of finite type: the composite $U\to X\to S$ is locally of finite type, and cancellation gives the assertion, both by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e),(f). The target $Y$ is locally Noetherian by the affine-chart argument of Step 2. Its actual completed stalk map is the isomorphism $g$ of Step 6, so [lem-trf-completed-stalk-isomorphism-etale] gives an open neighbourhood $W\ni u$ on which $f$ is etale, and an isomorphism $\kappa(y)\to\kappa(u)$. Replace $U$ by $W$. The map to $X$ remains etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation], since the open immersion $W\hookrightarrow U$ is etale. Its residue field map is still that of Step 1. The local ring at $u$, its maximal ideal, and both completed maps are unchanged by restriction, so the congruence modulo $\mathfrak m_u^N\widehat{\mathcal O}_{U,u}$ from Step 3 holds with exactly the original $\varphi$. This supplies both elementary etale neighbourhoods and the requested approximation.
